reasoning:
I'm weighing whether to commit to deleting grasp_end and merging it into grasp_point, loosening the grasp-frame detection threshold, and rewriting subgoal rules accordingly. The score looked perfect, but I'm second-guessing whether grasp_end is truly redundant, since the end class can only be recovered from the stored coordinate if the peg hasn't shifted after a failed pick attempt.

I'm leaning toward a conservative decision: keep grasp_end since a displaced peg after a failed pick would make it unrecoverable, but still accept the grasp-frame threshold clarification and the subgoal rule rewording, leaving the rule that depends on grasp_end untouched. That gives minimal, defensible edits rather than fully following the report's suggestion.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: choose A, pick up the peg by grasping one end, and point at grasp_point, i.e. the coordinates of the peg end (head or tail, matching grasp_end) that the demonstration gripper closed on, as that end appears in the current scene. Write grasp_point, grasp_end and insert_side at this step.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: choose A, pick up the peg by grasping one end, and point at the peg end (head or tail) nearest the demonstration gripper in the demonstration frame where the gripper is lowest and the fingers have first dropped from 100% open toward closed, at that end's coordinates in the current start-of-execution scene. Write grasp_point, grasp_end and insert_side at this step (grasp_point is this same point).

edits.modify_from: and the fingers have just gone from 100% open to about 22% open;
edits.modify_to: and the fingers have first dropped from 100% open toward closed (about 22% open, or a frame at about 50% while still closing);
(lowest height, fingers first dropped from 100% open toward closed, ~22% or ~50% while closing)

edits.modify_from: and the fingers go from 100% open to about 22% open:
edits.modify_to: and the fingers first drop from 100% open toward closed (about 22% open; a frame at about 50% on the way down also counts as the grasp frame):

edits.modify_from: whichever of peg head / peg tail is nearest the gripper at the moment the fingers close.
edits.modify_to: whichever of peg head / peg tail is nearest the gripper in the frame where the fingers first drop from 100% open toward closed (about 22%, or about 50% on the way down).

revision.refused: The deletion of grasp_end on both sides, and the rewrites of rules 3 and 4 that depend on it, stay out. The report's argument that the end class is recoverable from grasp_point holds only while the pegs lie where they lay at start of execution; the one situation in which grasp_end would ever be read is a failed or dropped pick, and that is exactly the situation in which the peg may have been displaced, so the entry nearest the stored point can then be the wrong end. The fact 'which end the demonstration closed on' is therefore not recovered by any later step when it is needed, and it is a different fact from the stored coordinate, so keeping it does not hold one fact twice. What is committed is the report's clarification of the grasp frame (a ~50% closing frame counts), applied consistently to grasp_point and grasp_end on both sides, and the rewording of rule 1 in terms of the demonstration rather than a memory that is still empty at that step.
